subject: Scope addendum & rate smoothing for Q1 capacity top-up
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@nexushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexus Health Procurement <procure@nexushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q1 capacity top-up + smoothing on new rate (order form attached)

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran numbers with our platform team and want to add an incremental 120k token-months for Q1 (projected burst to support a proof-of-concept). We prefer not to have a one-off price spike; can Redwood propose a smoothing option that phases the new per-token rate over 3 months (so our budget modelling isn't hit all at once)?

Attached is our (draft) order form with the quantities. High level asks:
- Add 120k token-months Jan–Mar 2026
- Cap unit increase to 15% month-over-month (smoothing acceptable)
- Billing proration for mid-month activation
- Confirmation that data separation for POC logs will remain in dedicated tenant (we need an audit trail)

Can legal redline the MSA/orderform and send the DocuSign when ready? We have procurement and finance on copy.

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager, Nexus Health
procure@nexushealth.com
(415) 555-0191

Attachment: proposed_orderform_nexus_Q1.pdf (1 page, table of quantities)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@nexushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Q1 capacity top-up + smoothing on new rate (order form attached)

Sam —

Appreciate the clear asks and the attachment. We're happy to support the POC burst. Quick notes:
- Smoothing: we can structure a 3-month phased rate increase as you suggested (we'll provide exact unit pricing options).
- Proration: standard proration applies; we'll call out mid-month activation explicitly in the order form.
- Data isolation: Nexus tenant will remain logically separated; I'll have our security/ops add a short note confirming audit log retention and access control.

I'll loop legal to prepare a short amendment (MSA addendum + order form) with the billing proration language and a temporary SLO for burst capacity. Laura, Jordan — can you review and incorporate: billing proration, a temporary cap-lift clause for burst, and a one-time rollback if POC fails within 30 days?

Target: send redline back to Nexus by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_orderform_nexus_Q1.pdf (embedded earlier)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Nexus add-on — legal redline request

Laura —

Forwarding Nexus request. Key items to include in the amendment redline:
1) Billing proration language for mid-cycle activation (explicit example: start date + pro-rata formula).
2) "Rollback" clause: if the POC is terminated within 30 days, customer can request a one-time credit that rebalances consumption to pre-topup baseline (limit to one occurrence).
3) Temporary SLO: we want a documented throughput allowance for burst months and a statement that Redwood will prioritize capacity within the dedicated pool; don't commit to firm SLA for burst but provide service-level expectations.
4) Data isolation & logs: short clause confirming tenant-level separation and audit log retention for 90 days, plus contact for audit log exports.
5) Signature lines: include both procurement and technical approver fields to speed countersign.

Laura — can you attach a draft redline and track changes? Also flag any commercial/legal risk with the smoothing language (we prefer not to accept open-ended tier guarantees).

Thanks — Marcus

Attachment: proposed_orderform_nexus_Q1.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 14:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexus add-on — legal redline request

Marcus / Jordan —

Thanks — I reviewed Nexus's order form. I prepared a redline of the MSA and a short amendment template (attached: redline_MSA_v2.docx). High-level edits and comments below (will track in the doc):

1) Proration: we will add the explicit pro-rata formula (daily proration from activation date) and an example row in the order form. This is straightforward.

2) Smoothing: do NOT commit to a percentage cap in the MSA. We can offer a commercial schedule in the order form Appendix A (e.g., month1 = $X, month2 = $Y, month3 = $Z) with a one-time permitted adjustment. That keeps contractual exposure limited.

3) Rollback / Credit: Acceptable as a one-time credit tied to documented termination within 30 days; cap credit to the incremental fee paid for the top-up months. We'll add a requirement for written notice within 10 business days of termination and an invoice audit right.

4) Data isolation & audit logs: propose 90-day audit log retention (per request). Add: "Redwood will provide export of tenant audit logs within 5 business days upon written request and subject to standard export fees." If Nexus needs longer retention, we need a commercial add-on.

5) Temporary SLO language: suggest non-binding service expectations (e.g., target P95 latency for bursts) with explicit statement that dedicated pool prioritization is best-effort during capacity contention. Do not expose full SLA targets in an amendment; point to the existing SLA schedule in the MSA and add a temporary Exhibit describing burst allowances.

6) Approvers & Signatures: recommend adding procurement and technical approver fields in the order form; also include the PO number field so finance can tie invoices.

Risks/notes:
- Avoid open-ended percentage caps or rolling credits.
- If Nexus insists on stronger rollback rights or longer log retention, route to commercial for pricing offsets.

Next steps: I will send the tracked redline to you both and to Nexus procurement. Marcus — confirm if we should include a 3-month priced schedule (I drafted conservative numbers in Appendix A).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: redline_MSA_v2.docx (MSA with tracked changes, amendment template)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@nexushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexus Health Procurement <procure@nexushealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Scope addendum & rate smoothing for Q1 capacity top-up

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. Nexus is okay with the approach Laura outlined: we prefer an explicit 3-month priced schedule in Appendix A rather than an open percentage cap. The rollback credit language is acceptable with the 10-business-day notice and invoice audit right.

Please send the final amendment and order form to our procurement inbox (procure@nexushealth.com) with DocuSign. Finance will route the PO after countersignature. Also include the audit log export contact in the amendment text.

If you can send DocuSign by Friday EOD, we will aim to have the signed PO the following week.

Best —
Sam

Attachment: none
